newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end lower, correction continues.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end lower, correction continues.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed lower, as the sloppy results of the Treasury's 10-year note auction spurred the market to further corrective losses, traders and analysts said.
"It was one of the sloppiest I've seen in quite awhile," Barrett Lewald, senior financial futures strategist at Lind-Waldock Inc, said.
The average yield was at 6.74 percent, with the bid-to-cover at 1.86 and non-comp bids at $383 million.
June T-bonds immediately fell to 109-08/32, leaving many traders bracing themselves for a break below 109-06/32.
September Eurodollars edged through support at 93.83. Key support is pegged at 93.80.
Traders were expecting a drop to 109-06/32, last Thursday's low, given the fact the much-awaited Beige Book was released only 15 minutes after the auction results.

One floor trader said June T-bonds decisively broke below last Friday's low of 109-14/32, despite earlier buying. He said a drop through 109-06/32 would have encouraged the contract to test the 108-20/32 area in the near term.
However, the Beige Book's comments dampened the downward momentum, and lifted June T-bonds to 109-15/32.
According to the Beige Book, which was released from the eighth district, the U.S. economy expanded moderately over the past two months.
Fed policymakers will use the Beige Book to consider whether to raise rates again on May 20.
The Beige Book also said U.S. wage and retail pressures were generally subdued and that the labor market was tight with "a few" new reports of upward wage pressure.
Lewald said underlying concerns such as the details in the U.S. budget agreement were weighing on the bond and Eurodollar futures markets.
"The bloom is off the rose as far as the budget deal is concerned," he said. "It's all well and good to have an announcement, but the details are not forthcoming."
On Friday, the White House and Republicans in Congress anounced a five-year balanced-budget agreement.

Lewald also said fears the dollar may be topping out in the intermediate-term was diminishing positive sentiment. The dollar weakened on talk that the U.S., Japan and Germany would enter the market to sell dollar/yen.
A decline in the dollar could lead foreign investors to sell U.S. Treasuries and other dollar-denominated assets, analysts said.

At the end of pit trade, June T-bonds were off 25/32 at 109-10/32, September T-bills were off 0.035 at 94.43, September Eurodollars were off 0.03 at 93.84 and December Eurodollars were down 0.05 at 93.61. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
